statement: As summarized by Sarparast et al. (2022), three other antidepressants were each tested before MDMA in one laboratory trial of 16 healthy adults, and they did not all act alike. Duloxetine (which blocks the serotonin and norepinephrine transporters) lowered nearly every effect ('any drug effect' 61.7% lower, drug liking 57.7% lower, closeness to others 83.1% lower, heart rate 57.4% lower), and reboxetine (a norepinephrine transporter blocker) lowered 'any drug effect' by 20.7% and heart rate by 26.2% but did not significantly lower drug liking or 'good drug effect'; with both, the MDMA peak was higher (duloxetine +14.6%, reboxetine +17.8%). Bupropion (which blocks the norepinephrine and dopamine transporters), taken for 7 days, did not lower the ratings: the areas under the curves of 'any drug effect', 'good drug effect', 'high' and liking over 8 hours were 36.7 to 46.1% higher, and the review says it prolonged the effects, while heart rate was 38.7% lower; the MDMA peak was 14.3% higher, the 24-hour exposure 33.1% higher and the peak of the metabolite HMMA 75.9% lower. So where the ratings were lowered (duloxetine, reboxetine) the peak MDMA level was still 15 to 18% higher, and where they were not (bupropion) the exposure over 24 hours was 33.1% higher. The review's authors say it is plausible, without data, that bupropion with MDMA raises the risk of seizures, stimulant toxicity or serotonin syndrome, since both are stimulants that lower the seizure threshold and raise each other's blood levels. People can feel little from an amount for several reasons (a slow start, tolerance, a weaker or different product, bodies that differ, or a medicine that blunts the effect) and some take more; none of the trials gave more MDMA once the effects were blunted, so what happens then was not measured. The percentages are the review's, partly read off graphs; the three trials come from one laboratory group and were not read for this library; and none followed people on long-term treatment.
plain: Other antidepressants did not all act alike. In single lab trials of 16 healthy people each, duloxetine and reboxetine muted MDMA's effects, and the MDMA level in the blood was a little higher (about 15 to 18 percent at the peak). Bupropion did not mute the effects: ratings were as high or higher than without it, and the MDMA level was higher too (about 14 percent at the peak and 33 percent over the day), while heart rate rose less. Some people feel little from an amount and take more, for reasons such as a slow start, tolerance, a weaker or different product, bodies that differ, or a medicine that mutes the effect. No trial tested what happens then. The review's authors guess, without data, that bupropion and MDMA together might raise the risk of seizures. These numbers come second-hand, from a 2022 review.
population: Healthy adult volunteers in three single laboratory trials of 16 people each, as summarized by Sarparast et al. (2022)
exposure: An antidepressant taken before MDMA (study conditions as listed in the review: duloxetine or reboxetine as a single dose or two doses within a day; bupropion for several days; MDMA by mouth)
comparator: The same people given a dummy treatment before MDMA
outcome: Rated effects of MDMA, heart rate, blood pressure, catecholamines, and blood concentrations of MDMA and its metabolite HMMA
magnitude: As summarized by Sarparast et al. (2022), changes against placebo before MDMA: duloxetine 'any drug effect' -61.7%, liking -57.7%, closeness -83.1%, heart rate -57.4% (all p<.001), MDMA peak +14.6%, exposure to 6 hours +16.2%, HMMA peak -40.5%; reboxetine 'any drug effect' -20.7% (p<.01), heart rate -26.2% (p<.05), liking -10.0% and good drug effect -15.2% (not significant), MDMA peak +17.8%, exposure to 24 hours +8.1% (p<.05); bupropion area under the curve of ratings over 8 hours +34.0 to +46.1% (p<.05), peak ratings +5.6 to +17.1% (not marked significant), heart rate -38.7% (p<.001), MDMA peak +14.3%, exposure to 24 hours +33.1% (p<.001), HMMA peak -75.9%.

evidence.locator: Table 6, duloxetine and reboxetine rows; Results › MDMA › Serotonin reuptake inhibitors and MDMA, 2nd paragraph; Reboxetine and MDMA
evidence.extracted: Duloxetine (n=16) lowered nearly every effect of MDMA: 'any drug effect' 61.7%, drug liking 57.7% and closeness to others 83.1% (all p<.001), heart rate 57.4% and systolic pressure 63.5% (p<.001), and acute complaints 122.5% (p<.01; above 100% because, as the review says, complaints with duloxetine and MDMA were below the pre-drug baseline). Reboxetine (n=16) lowered 'any drug effect' by 20.7% (p<.01), closeness by 38.6% (p<.05), heart rate by 26.2% (p<.05) and systolic pressure by 46.5% (p<.001), but drug liking (-10.0%) and good drug effect (-15.2%) did not change significantly. Values with a tilde were read off graphs by the review's authors.

evidence.locator: Table 6, pharmacokinetic rows (Cmax, AUC) for each medicine; Results › MDMA, the paragraphs on bupropion, serotonin reuptake inhibitors, duloxetine and reboxetine
evidence.extracted: MDMA blood levels were higher with these medicines at the same time as effects were lower. Duloxetine: peak +14.6%, exposure to 6 hours +16.2%, HMMA peak 40.5% lower. Reboxetine: peak +17.8%, exposure to 24 hours +8.1% (p<.05). Bupropion: peak +14.3%, exposure to 24 hours +33.1% (p<.001), HMMA peak 75.9% lower. For comparison, carvedilol (+4.7%), clonidine (-2.9%), doxazosin (-1.6%) and methylphenidate (-3.5%) changed the peak by 5% or less, and memantine's level at 1 hour was 1.0% lower. Table 6 has no blood-level row for citalopram or fluoxetine.

evidence.locator: Table 6, bupropion rows (Physiological; Circulating catecholamines; Subjective); Results › MDMA › Bupropion and MDMA; Discussion › Pharmacodynamic interactions-MDMA, 2nd paragraph
evidence.extracted: Bupropion XR (n=16; taken for 7 days, with the amount stepped up, as listed in Table 5) did not blunt the rated effects: peak ratings of any drug effect, good effect, 'high', liking and 'stimulated' were 5.6 to 17.1% higher (no significance marks), and the areas under the rating curves over 8 hours were 36.7 to 46.1% higher for any drug effect, good effect, 'high' and liking (p<.05) and 34.0% higher for 'stimulated' (no mark), while heart rate was 38.7% lower (p<.001) and norepinephrine 65.6% lower (p<.05). The Results say bupropion significantly prolonged the positive mood effects of MDMA, and the Discussion that it prolonged the subjective effects and heightened the positive mood effects, and calls it plausible, without data, that bupropion with MDMA raises the risk of seizures, stimulant toxicity or serotonin syndrome because both are stimulants that can lower the seizure threshold and raise each other's blood levels. Its surveillance paragraph gives bupropion the highest unadjusted odds ratio of death of any antidepressant (2.82; see the claim on reports).

evidence.locator: Table 5; Results, 2nd paragraph; Discussion, 2nd paragraph; Discussion › Pharmacodynamic interactions-MDMA, 2nd paragraph
evidence.extracted: The 13 MDMA trials in Table 5 had 8 to 16 healthy adults each, nearly all double-blind counterbalanced crossovers; the medicine was given as a single dose or two doses within a day in 9 of the 13 and for 3 to 11 days in the other 4 (doxazosin, paroxetine, bupropion, fluoxetine). The Discussion says the trials came primarily from one laboratory group, that participants were young healthy adults, and that the studies are limited in their extrapolation to settings where medicines are taken daily for months or years. The percentage changes are the review's own calculation, and the review did not appraise the risk of bias of any included study.

risk_of_bias.note: The primary trials were not read for this library; the review that reports them appraised none of them and is rated critically low on AMSTAR 2 (study card); some values were read off graphs.

inconsistency.note: Not rated: each medicine rests on one trial.

indirectness.note: Second-hand: numbers come through a review, from healthy volunteers given the medicine for hours to days.

imprecision.note: 16 people per medicine; the review gives no intervals.

grade.reasoning: The primary trials are double-blind, counterbalanced crossovers and start high (METHODS 6.3); the claim reaches them only through a systematic review that did not appraise them, so risk of bias -1 (not appraisable) and indirectness -1 (second-hand) are applied, with imprecision -1 for 16 people each. Certainty very low. Status single-study: each medicine was tested once, three trials from one laboratory group. Stays at draft because it rests only on the review (METHODS 12, brief). The claim says what was measured, never what to do.

verification.flag_note: Rests only on Sarparast et al. (2022) as summarized, until the primary trials are read: duloxetine (Hysek et al., 2012, doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0036476), reboxetine (Hysek et al., 2011, doi 10.1038/clpt.2011.78) and bupropion (Schmid et al., 2015, doi 10.1124/jpet.114.222356) have no reference records. The editor may join this claim with the claim on SSRIs.
